title: MASIM - multi-array scheduler for SIMD logic-in-memory to reduce copy instructions
problem: SIMD logic-in-memory (LIM) systems require frequent data copying between memory and processing arrays, creating bottlenecks. Scheduling across multiple arrays to minimize data movement is a complex optimization problem.
motivation: Intelligent scheduling that exploits multiple processing arrays can reduce redundant copy instructions and improve data locality, thereby reducing energy consumption and improving throughput.
method: MASIM provides a multi-array scheduling framework that orchestrates computation across multiple SIMD processing arrays while minimizing data copy operations through intelligent task assignment and data placement strategies.
key_novelty: Multi-array scheduling approach for SIMD logic-in-memory systems that explicitly optimizes for reducing copy instruction overhead.
contributions: Multi-array scheduling framework for SIMD LIM architectures
28% energy savings through reduced data movement
Methodology for optimizing task distribution across heterogeneous processing arrays
limitations: Energy savings may vary significantly depending on workload characteristics and array configuration, limiting generalization across diverse systems.
